glossary.def: Share of queries with at least one relevant result in the top k. A conventional definition; no vendor evaluator page in scope names it.
Relevant results in the top k divided by all relevant documents for the query. Shows whether the evidence reached the prompt.
Relevant results in the top k divided by k. Unstable across queries because it depends on how many relevant documents exist.
Retrieved documents with no relevance judgment. Foundry reports `holes` and `holes_ratio` because unjudged items distort rank metrics.
RAGAS metric: the mean of precision at k over ranks that hold a relevant chunk, so putting relevant chunks first raises it.
RAGAS metric: claims in the reference answer attributable to the retrieved context divided by all claims in the reference. Needs a reference.
RAGAS metric: share of response claims that are wrong against the reference while attributable to retrieved context. Lower is better.
A model that scores or compares outputs against a rubric. Reliable only after calibration against human labels.
Asking a judge which of two answers is better. Suited to ranking two candidates and run in both orders to cancel position bias.
Hamel Husain's method: one principal expert gives pass/fail verdicts with written critiques, then the judge prompt is iterated until it agrees.
People need criteria to grade outputs, but grading outputs changes the criteria. Expect to revise a rubric while labelling.
A Foundry evaluator (preview) made of weighted scoring dimensions applied by an LLM judge, written by hand or generated from the agent's context.
A Foundry evaluator such as `builtin.output_quality` that batches several criteria into one judge call and passes only if every applicable component passes.
The aggregate share of responses in which a safety evaluator detects undesired content.
A non-production environment with production-like resources, used to run red team scans without real side effects.
A confidence interval for a proportion that behaves better than the normal approximation for small samples and rates near 0 or 100%.
With zero failures in n independent runs, the 95% upper bound on the failure rate is about 3/n.
Sending a small share of users to a new version, with stop-loss metrics, before wider rollout.
Test cases generated by a model from documents or an agent definition. Needs review, a provenance tag and regeneration when instructions change.
A suite that checks the system still does what it did. It should sit near 100% and can block a release, unlike a capability eval.

claims.text: Capability evals start at a low pass rate while regression evals should sit near 100%, and high-pass capability tasks can graduate into the regression suite.
Foundry continuous evaluation (preview) defaults to 100 runs per hour (`max_hourly_runs`) and skips runs when the cap is reached.
Anthropic advises that 20 to 50 simple tasks drawn from real failures is a great start for an agent eval set.
GAIA has 466 questions and withholds answers to 300 of them to power a leaderboard.
A secondary source reports OpenAI stopped evaluating on SWE-bench Verified in February 2026; the primary page could not be fetched.
Foundry evaluation runs allow at most 2 MB per row and 100,000 rows per batch evaluation.
Foundry synthetic datasets have two task types, Simple QnA (query and ground_truth) and Simulation seed (test_case_description), and `max_samples` accepts 1 to 1,000.
With only 8 relevant documents, a perfect system scores at most 0.4 precision at k=20.
MRR for first-relevant ranks 1, 3, none and 2 is (1 + 0.333 + 0 + 0.5) / 4 = 0.458.
For relevance 3, 2, 0, 1 nDCG is 0.985 with linear gain and 0.993 with exponential gain, so scores differ across libraries.

Foundry's Document Retrieval evaluator (`builtin.document_retrieval`) returns ndcg@3, xdcg@3, fidelity, top1_relevance, top3_max_relevance, holes and holes_ratio, with a label range defaulting to 0 to 4.

RAGAS answer relevancy generates N questions from the response (default 3) and averages cosine similarity to the user input; the class is `AnswerRelevancy` while the docs title says Response Relevancy.
ragas 0.4.3 was released on 2026-01-13, and the legacy `SingleTurnSample` API is deprecated in 0.4 and removed in 1.0.
Foundry composite evaluators use default pass thresholds of 3 on 1 to 5 scales and 1 on 0/1 scales, and the primary result passes only if every applicable component passes.

Agent evaluators have limited support for Azure AI Search, Bing Grounding, Bing Custom Search, SharePoint Grounding, Code Interpreter, Fabric Data Agent and Web Search, so avoid tool_call_accuracy, tool_input_accuracy, tool_output_utilization, tool_call_success and groundedness there.
azure-ai-evaluation 1.18.8 was released on 2026-10-09, and new cloud evaluation uses azure-ai-projects 2.2.0 or later (latest 2.8.0 on 2026-10-05).

Custom evaluators (preview) come in three kinds: code-based `grade(sample, item)` returning 0.0 to 1.0, prompt-based JSON with `result` and `reason`, and endpoint-based returning `score`, `reason`, `status`.
Risk and safety evaluators include prohibited actions and sensitive data leakage (agents only, preview) and report an aggregate defect rate.
Foundry recommends a rubric evaluator, weighted dimensions applied by an LLM judge and generated from an agent's name, instructions and tools, as the primary agent evaluation measure.
In MT-Bench, GPT-4 exceeded 80% agreement with humans and reached 85% against 81% human-human agreement in the non-tie setup.
On MT-Bench math grading the default judge failed 14 of 20, chain-of-thought 6 of 20 and a reference-guided judge 3 of 20.
Swap consistency under the default prompt was GPT-4 65.0%, GPT-3.5 46.2% and Claude-v1 23.8%, and a few-shot judge raised GPT-4 to 77.5% at about 4x prompt cost.
Reordering answers let Vicuna-13B beat ChatGPT on 66 of 80 queries with ChatGPT as the judge.
The repetitive-list verbosity attack fooled Claude-v1 and GPT-3.5 91.3% of the time and GPT-4 8.7% of the time.
GPT-4 favoured itself with about 10% higher win rate and Claude-v1 about 25%, which the paper called inconclusive; later work links self-recognition to self-preference.
tau-bench grades by comparing the final database state with the annotated goal state, over 115 retail and 50 airline tasks.
tau-bench pass^k is the chance all k trials succeed, estimated as C(c,k)/C(n,k) per task, and pass^1 equals pass@1.
gpt-4o with function calling scored about 61% retail and 35% airline at pass^1, and about 25% in retail at pass^8.
The Codex paper's abstract reports 28.8% of HumanEval problems solved with one sample and 70.2% with 100 samples per problem (its Table 2 lists 72.3% at 100 samples for the 12B model).
Clustered standard errors can be more than 3x the naive standard error, and 95% intervals use mean plus or minus 1.96 x SE.
The 95% half-width for an 80% pass rate is 11.1, 7.8, 5.5, 3.9 and 2.5 points at n = 50, 100, 200, 400 and 1,000 (computed).
Foundry's compare view marks a change strong at p <= 0.001 and weak at 0.001 < p <= 0.05.
The AI Red Teaming Agent defines attack success rate as successful attacks divided by total attacks, uses PyRIT, is text only, and its local mode is preview.

Local red team scans need azure-ai-evaluation[redteam] and Python 3.10 to 3.13, default num_objectives to 10, and one objective per four categories with four strategies plus baseline gives 20 attack-response pairs.

Cloud agentic red teaming supports Foundry prompt agents and hosted container agents with Azure tool calls, and does not support function tool calls, workflow agents, non-Foundry agents, browser automation, connected agents or computer use.

The microsoft/ai-agent-evals GitHub Action (preview) takes agent-ids as name:version, treats the first agent as baseline unless baseline-agent-id is set, and reports confidence intervals and a significance test.
OpenAI's Evals platform becomes read-only on 2026-10-31 and is scheduled to shut down on 2026-11-30, with Promptfoo named as the migration path.
With zero failures in n runs the rule of three bounds the 95% upper limit on the failure rate near 3/n.
Azure Machine Learning traffic mirroring caps mirrored traffic at 50%, allows one shadow deployment per endpoint and is not supported on Kubernetes online endpoints.
Samples per arm to detect a gap near an 80% pass rate (alpha 0.05, power 0.80, unpaired) are about 251 for 10 points, 1,004 for 5 points and 2,788 for 3 points (computed).
